# ccc-autocode-neo PROD PRD v0.5.0

## Executive Decision

> [!abstract]
> Build `ccc-autocode-neo` as a hybrid engine: Dagu owns a small static outer graph of phases, and a new procedural Python dispatcher inside the dispatch phase owns the chunk graph, leases, worktrees, and merges. Truth stays gate-owned exactly as in Autocode-Lite. State is a hash-chained append-only JSONL WorkLedger (source of truth) plus a disposable SQLite/WAL query index. Build the proof-kernel transplant and state core first, then a serial dispatcher that already runs through the parallel code paths, then turn parallelism on.

`ccc-autocode-neo` is the first full PRD-to-product autonomous coding engine in Ryan's stack: it ingests a source PRD, clarifies it interactively, researches it, synthesizes an end-to-end implementation spec, decomposes that spec into a dependency-aware chunk DAG, dispatches chunks to OpenCode/Ralph-style workers in isolated git worktrees, proves every chunk with an independent gate, validates the whole product with a MEGATEST plus a false-green negation layer, repairs bounded failures, and produces a final adjudication with a sealed audit capsule. Autocode-Lite is the proven serial proof lane that supplies the trust kernel; it is not the engine, and this PRD never treats it as already parallel.

The thirteen required architecture decisions are all made in this document. None is left open. This document is deliberately self-contained: every fact, constraint, constant, schema, and decision needed to understand and build the system is stated in this file, and no external note is required reading (the provenance appendix names archival sources for audit only). Version history, briefly: v0.1.0 was the original adjudicated draft; v0.2.0 applied the first adversarial-review patch (SQLite writer matrix, reboot-safe ledger ordering, Tier-3 cascade and lease/fence lifecycle completion, product-repo bootstrap and runtime capability-pack tasks, ship converted to an operator-confirmed proposal); v0.2.1 applied the second review cycle (Lamport logical clock replacing timestamp ordering, cascade crash-recovery bracket, mandatory `--no-ff` merges making `revert -m 1` provably correct, collision-free branch namespaces, a separate gate concurrency budget, and NEO-M2-009 owning the external review); v0.3.0 is the contract-closure edition: it freezes trusted-repository admission, approved-remote egress, operator-confirmed publication, replay-safe state and side effects, closed proof schemas, total lifecycles, a 23-task implementation DAG, eight global acceptance rows, and separate live SHIP and truthful-failure evidence. v0.4.0 closes the remaining implementation gaps found by the first blind post-apply review: trusted-repository-only admission, exact research neutralization, total remote-call and Dagu transactions, closed clarification and operator-query surfaces, one gate-fold owner, ordered process locks, mechanical external review, release-scoped evidence, a committed truthful-failure candidate, a non-self-referential handoff, deterministic merge planning, and exact task/proof parity. v0.5.0 is the bounded convergence repair: it unifies requirement IDs, closes trusted-repository and handoff schemas, makes negative controls executable, repairs intake/adjudication/gate state contracts, removes unsafe pre-lock ledger writes, and resolves the final query, review, Dagu, and truthful-failure contradictions.

What to build first: the NEO-M0 tasks — the neo repo scaffold, the schema pack with drift-parity tests, the WorkLedger writer and replay projector, and the run-namespaced proof-kernel transplant. Nothing else in the engine is trustworthy until those exist.


## Problem Statement

Autocode-Lite proves that one bounded prompt can be turned into one proven deliverable with honest verdicts: an independent gate re-runs a sealed proof spec in a clean workspace copy and writes `.autocode/gate.json`, and the workledger records gate truth rather than worker narration. But Lite is deliberately serial and single-tenant: `max_active_steps: 1`, one attached OpenCode slot, one workspace, one workledger file, and no concept of a product larger than one lane run. Ryan's actual need — sketched in the 2026-07-05 diagram — is a whole-product engine: take a real PRD, clarify and research it, compile it into an executable spec of many dependency-aware chunks, run those chunks in parallel with the same proof discipline Lite proved, integrate the results, validate the entire product end to end, repair what is repairable within bounds, and adjudicate honestly with a durable blackbox record. Today nothing in the stack does chunk decomposition, dependency scheduling, parallel worker isolation, product-level validation, or global state. Building "bigger Lite" by loosening its serial assumptions would silently break its trust model; neo must be a new engine that transplants Lite's proof kernel as an organ.

## Product Vision

A single command starts a run: `neo run --prd path/to/prd.md`. The engine walks the PRD through interactive clarification into an enhanced PRD, plans and executes bounded deep research into a cited implementation research report, and synthesizes an end-to-end implementation spec whose main unit is the CHUNK — isolated, scoped, dependency-DAG-ready, with `depends_on` and `provides`. A dispatcher compiles the chunk DAG, then leases ready chunks to workers in isolated git worktrees, serial at first and parallel per dependencies at maturity. Every chunk is proven by the transplanted independent gate; passing chunks merge in deterministic order onto a per-run integration branch; regression runs before each merge advance. When the coding loop declares success, the engine does not believe it: full e2e validation runs a dynamic AI review, tests and linting, test-deficiency review, and the MEGATEST simulation, with a negation layer that plants defects to prove the tests can actually fail. Bounded repair handles fixable failures; unfixable ones produce a full postmortem. A passing final adjudication seals the capsule but does not publish. A post-capsule planner may create a publication proposal only for SHIP; one fresh, exact operator confirmation authorizes one publication transaction. The entire run is replayable from a sealed, hash-chained WorkLedger capsule. The operator can walk away from a running engine and later reconstruct exactly what happened, why, and at what cost, from artifacts alone.

## Scope

Version 1 scope (through milestone M3) covers: the neo repo and schema pack; the WorkLedger event log, replay projector, and SQLite index; the run-namespaced proof-kernel transplant; PRD intake, interactive Q&A, and enhanced-PRD sealing; the research plan/report lane with budget caps and injection quarantine; e2e implementation spec synthesis and chunk DAG compilation with static validation; the dispatcher with leases, fencing, worktrees, ordered merges, and tiered failure handling; worker adapters for OpenCode/Ralph (required) behind the adapter protocol; per-chunk gates and product-level integration validation; MEGATEST with fixture `neo-e2e-fixture-001` in LLM-free and live modes; the false-green negation layer; bounded repair, postmortem, final adjudication, and capsule sealing; Dagu outer-graph wiring and a backup-first deploy path; and an operator status surface. Parallelism scales from 1 to a bounded pool (2–3) to the full parallel engine within v1's charter.

## Non-Goals

Neo v1 does not build: multi-host distributed dispatch (single-host run root is the v1 rule; cross-host workers are an M4+ increment), Dagu's distributed coordinator/worker mode, Dagu's built-in agent-harness steps, any cloud or SaaS orchestration component, a web UI beyond a minimal status view, autonomous write access to KnR-Vault, autonomous `git push` to shared remotes before a ship adjudication, vault-embedding-backed semantic memory, trading-domain execution of any kind, mutation testing as a day-one dependency (deferred, see the dependency matrix), fine-grained per-token cost optimization (capture costs, do not optimize yet), and generalizing the engine for other operators. Neo also does not absorb the deferred Autocode-Lite P3 product-path follow-up; that boundary stays intact.

## Design Principles

1. Gate-owned truth, always. No worker narration, coordinator log line, or checkbox is ever proof. Every chunk verdict comes from an independent gate re-running a sealed proof in a clean copy, and every product verdict comes from the validation lane. This is Lite's core invariant, preserved without exception.
2. The ledger is the run. If an event is not in the WorkLedger, it did not happen; if replaying the ledger cannot reproduce the derived state, the run is degraded and cannot ship.
3. Serial is a configuration, not an architecture. The M1 serial dispatcher runs through the identical lease/worktree/merge code paths as full parallel; there is no separate serial mode to later throw away.
4. Isolation before concurrency. No two workers ever share a workspace, a branch, a slot config, or a write boundary. Overlap is rejected at spec-compile time and caught again at gate and merge time.
5. Fail closed, bounded, and loud. Every retry, repair, and budget has an enforced ceiling with a named enforcement point. Exhaustion routes to postmortem, never to silent looping. Authoritative writes that fail abort the actor.
6. Untrusted by default. Research content, worker output, fetched pages, and prior-attempt lessons are data, not instructions. Everything injected into a worker prompt passes the neutralization fence.
7. Local-first primitives. JSONL, SQLite/WAL, filesystem locks, git worktrees, launchd/Dagu. A new dependency must prove existing stack pieces cannot do the job.
8. Reversible by construction. Backup-first deploys, per-run integration branches that never touch `main` before ship adjudication, archives over deletions, and additive-only schema evolution.
9. Human-shaped observability. The operator must be able to answer "what is happening, what failed, why, and what did it cost" from the status surface and ledger alone, days later.
10. Small honest steps. Every milestone ends with a named verification command and observed result; no milestone is "done" by assertion.

## Current Autocode-Lite Baseline

Autocode-Lite is a proven serial proof lane, not the full parallel engine. The live graph in `dags/autocode-graph.yaml` is `precheck -> spec_forge -> plan -> spec_plan_gate -> no_model_preflight -> run_loop -> packet_write -> verify_run_artifacts -> lane_verdict` with `max_active_steps: 1` and `timeout_sec: 1800`. Retry default is 3 clean attempts (`RALPH_MAX_ITERATIONS`), the enforced ceiling is 10 (`run_loop.py` rejects anything outside `[1, 10]` before worker spend), and the worker attempt timeout is 900 seconds (`WORKER_TIMEOUT_SEC`, read in `run_loop.py` and enforced via the worker subprocess timeout). The gate copies the workspace into a fresh temp directory, runs sealed acceptance/regression/typed proofs there with process-group kill on timeout, enforces allowed/forbidden path policy, and writes `.autocode/gate.json` as the only authoritative verdict. `packet_write.py` emits the workledger row from gate truth, and `verify_run_artifacts.py` refuses success unless gate, run-loop result, trace, and ledger row all agree.

Single-tenancy is structural, not incidental. The lane binds to one OpenCode slot (`slot-01` at `:11500`); when `AUTOCODE_MODEL` is set, `model_routing.py` rewrites the shared slot config on disk and restarts the slot via `launchctl kickstart` (`model_routing.py:731-810`), which would yank a live slot out from under any concurrent run. The workledger is one flat JSONL file appended without locking, and `verify_run_artifacts.py` finds "its" row by scanning for the latest line matching the workspace path — a heuristic that misattributes rows under concurrent writers. Attempt archiving, promotion staging, and source snapshots all assume exclusive ownership of one workspace's `.autocode/` tree.

Two live schema/code drifts were verified in this run and matter for the transplant. First, `schemas/run_event.schema.json` allows only 8 `stage` enum values while `trace_event.py` `STAGES` has 10 — code emits `no_model_preflight` and `verify_run_artifacts` stages the schema would reject. Second, `schemas/gate.schema.json` declares `additionalProperties: false` without any `proofs` property, while `deliverable_gate.py` writes a `proofs` results block in the gate result structure (fail-template near line 259; typed-proof path near line 1113) once typed proofs exist — so a real passing gate.json fails strict validation against its own schema. Neither drift is caught by a parity test today. Neo inherits the lesson, not the bug.

What Lite does not have, verified against the repo file inventory: no dispatcher, no chunk or dependency-DAG concept, no lease or claim mechanism, no worktree isolation (attempt isolation is `shutil.copytree`), no multi-slot worker pool, no product-level e2e validation beyond one lane's acceptance, no global repair state machine, and no state store for PRDs, research, specs, chunks, or adjudications. Chunk-size and global repair-pass caps are advisory prose only — STATUS.md says so explicitly.

*Table 3: Proof-kernel transplant boundary with source evidence.*

The Q1 rolling-volatility lesson carries forward as doctrine: data-science chunks get staged input fixtures, locked formula semantics, explicit output shapes, tolerances, and gate-owned hidden baselines (Q1's expected value `0.02086722885939345` at ±1e-12 lives in a registry the worker never sees). Vague quantitative prompts fail; execution-grade contracts pass honestly.


## Operator and Runtime Fit

Neo is a local-first product for one operator. Each run keeps its authoritative ledger, SQLite projections, locks, and worktrees on one local APFS host; the NAS may receive only sealed cold artifacts. No planning-era hostname, listener, port, tool version, resource figure, or model route is present-day proof. The built product must rerun and seal the named capability, compatibility, resource, and route probes before it spends, schedules, executes, publishes, archives, or cleans up.
Trusted-repository admission is not operating-system containment. V1 workers may run only after the exact trust attestation, sanitized Git profile, approved-remote policy, protected-path exclusions, disclosure checks, and negative controls in the normative contract pass.

## Frozen Product Decisions

- **DEC-001 — trusted repository admission:** v1 accepts only repositories covered by a sealed operator trust attestation. This is admission control, not a claim of operating-system containment. Revocation blocks new execution.
- **DEC-002 — approved remote policy:** outbound model and research calls use a reusable sealed allowlist with deny-by-default data classes, redaction and disclosure evidence, expiry, and revocation. A local-only override remains valid.
- **DEC-003 — release evidence:** release requires one live successful SHIP run and a separate controlled live truthful-failure run, with different run IDs and independently verified capsules.
- **Portfolio-shape rule:** the top, middle, and bottom thirds are a guiding principle applied deterministically after ranking. Upward promotion requires sealed evidence; downward movement, quota balancing, and category-forced demotion are forbidden.

## Normative Technical Contract

This section controls over all overview prose and inherited historical descriptions. Every field, enum, invariant, default, transition, command, exit code, proof path, authority, failure rule, and policy below is fixed. Mechanical fixture values and JSON-Schema boilerplate are implementation work only when they preserve these semantics exactly.

### Shared schema, identity, and hashing rules

- Every persisted JSON contract is a closed root object with `schema_id` equal to its named contract and integer `schema_version: 1`. Nested authority-bearing objects are also closed. Map fields are explicitly declared maps rather than open accidental objects.
- `Id` is 1–128 characters and matches `^(?!.*\.lock$)[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$`; `RunId` additionally forbids `:`. `Sha256` is lowercase 64-hex. `GitOid` is lowercase 40- or 64-hex. `UtcMs` is RFC 3339 UTC with exactly milliseconds. `Usd` is a nonnegative JSON number that is an exact multiple of `0.000001`; arithmetic uses integer microdollars. `RelPath` is NFC-normalized POSIX relative, never absolute, empty, `.`, `..`, or NUL-containing. `AbsPath` is NFC-normalized absolute POSIX with no `.`, `..`, or NUL component. `GitRef` must pass `git check-ref-format` and may not end `.lock`.
- `ArtifactRef` is `{artifact_id: Id, schema_id: string, schema_version: integer >=1, path: RelPath, sha256: Sha256}`. `FileEntry` is `{path: RelPath, media_type: nonempty string, size_bytes: integer >=0, sha256: Sha256}`. Arrays that represent sets are duplicate-free and sorted by UTF-8 byte order.
- No artifact carries its own content digest. Every non-seal JSON artifact is validated, canonicalized with RFC 8785, and sealed by detached `artifact_seal.v1`; non-JSON artifacts use raw bytes. `artifact_seal.v1` and `capsule_seal.v1` are terminal detached witnesses: they never carry or require another seal, and consumers bind their exact content digest through `ArtifactRef.sha256`. The detached artifact seal has `seal_id`, `run_id`, artifact identity/schema/path/media type, canonicalization `rfc8785|raw_bytes`, content SHA-256, byte length, stable producer transaction ID, prior authorization event or null only for pre-ledger genesis input, seal time, and sealing actor. It never names the future event that will bind the seal. Any changed content gets a new artifact ID and seal.
- Removal, rename, retype, or a new required field requires a version bump and retained reader. Unknown newer versions stop replay and mark the run `DEGRADED`; no best-effort parse is permitted.
- Immutable artifacts never mutate. Derived operational projections such as `run_epoch_state.v1` and `publication_execution.v1` use append-only immutable revisions linked by `previous_revision_sha256`; WorkLedger replay always outranks the projection.
- Every schema gets at least one validating fixture and one targeted rejection fixture. The rejection fixture must exercise the named invariant rather than merely omit an arbitrary required field.

### WorkLedger event identity, authority, and replay matrix

Every authoritative event validates as `workledger_event.v1` with `schema_id`, integer `schema_version=1`, `event_id`, `run_id`, `manifest_sha256`, `epoch`, `logical_seq`, `actor_id`, `actor_incarnation_id`, `actor_seq`, `event_type`, `aggregate_type`, `aggregate_id`, `idempotency_key`, `durability="authoritative"`, `ts_wall`, `ts_mono`, `prev_hash`, `payload_schema_id`, integer `payload_schema_version>=1`, and closed typed payload. `payload_schema_id` and `payload_schema_version` identify the exact schema that validates the payload. `actor_id` is the stable logical role; `actor_incarnation_id` is unique per actor/epoch/process start. `actor_seq` begins zero and increases exactly one inside an incarnation. `logical_seq` is zero only when the event has no observed/causation event in the epoch; otherwise it is exactly one plus the maximum logical sequence among the causation event and every sealed input event the actor actually consumed. An actor may not claim an unconsumed observation. Physical clocks are diagnostic only.

Canonical event bytes are RFC 8785 over the complete envelope; no event embeds its own hash. `event_content_sha256` is the transient SHA-256 of those bytes. Segment link hash is the prior event's content hash, with each incarnation's first segment event using `prev_hash=manifest_sha256`; rotated segments continue from the prior segment's terminal event hash. `payload_sha256` is computed transiently for identity only. After sorting all valid stored events by canonical replay order, the canonical ledger head is the streaming fold `H0=SHA256(0x00 || raw_manifest_sha256)` and `Hn=SHA256(0x01 || H(n-1) || raw_event_content_sha256_n)`; the empty ledger head is H0. Late arrival that inserts before the current ordered watermark forces deterministic refold before FRESH. Deterministic identifiers are:

```text
idempotency_key = SHA256(RFC8785({run_id,event_type,aggregate_type,
                                  aggregate_id,semantic_transaction_id,
                                  semantic_step,input_precondition_hash}))
event_id = "evt-" + SHA256(RFC8785({run_id,actor_incarnation_id,actor_seq,
                                     event_type,aggregate_type,aggregate_id,
                                     idempotency_key,payload_sha256}))[0:32]
```

Side-effect payloads require stable `semantic_transaction_id`, `semantic_step`, and `input_precondition_hash` across retries. Exact duplicate ID plus byte-identical event is already applied. Reuse of an event ID or idempotency key with different bytes is `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and degrades the run. A distinct event proposing an already-satisfied transition is a no-op only where the matrix says so; otherwise it is illegal. Replay order is `(epoch,logical_seq,actor_id,actor_seq,event_id)`. Authoritative events append+fsync before their fact is acted on or acknowledged. Heartbeats are not events and never enter a WorkLedger segment, event order, canonical head, snapshot, capsule member set, or replay.

The normative chunk-state enum is `PENDING|READY|LEASED|RUNNING|WORKER_FINISHED|ATTEMPT_FAILED|REPAIR_PENDING|REPAIRING|GATE_PENDING|GATING|GATED|MERGE_PENDING|MERGED|FAILED|ABANDONED|BLOCKED_BY_DEP|BLOCKED_OPERATOR`. No implicit state exists. `REPAIR_PENDING` means worker/gate authority is closed and the durable repair trigger has not begun; `REPAIRING` means the repair coordinator has consumed that trigger and owns an active decision. They are distinct legal states; the removed invalid alias was bare `REPAIR`. A candidate-commit event is legal only from WORKER_FINISHED; a worker lease grant is legal only from READY.

| Event types | Sole legal emitter | Aggregate and legal fold | Durability | Duplicate/reducer rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run_started`, `repo_context_bound` | run controller | `CREATED -> PREPARING_REPO -> INTAKE_PENDING`; bind source/config/schema and sealed repository context | authoritative | identical no-op; changed binding degrades |
| `intake_started`, `intake_blocked`, `intake_resumed`, `intake_completed` | foreground intake controller | `INTAKE_PENDING -> INTAKE_ACTIVE -> INTAKE_BLOCKED|READY_TO_SUBMIT`; blocked resumes to active; completion binds enhanced PRD | authoritative | Q&A round and input digest exact; duplicate completion no-op |
| `dagu_submission_intent`, `dagu_submission_committed`, `dagu_submission_uncertain`, `dagu_submission_reconciled`, `dagu_execution_started` | run controller for submission; internal Dagu phase driver for execution start | `READY_TO_SUBMIT -> SUBMITTING -> SUBMITTED|SUBMISSION_UNCERTAIN`; reconcile uncertainty to `SUBMITTED|READY_TO_SUBMIT`; `SUBMITTED -> RUNNING` | authoritative | one external idempotency key and Dagu run ID; observe before retry |
| `run_resumed` | recovery controller holding both locks | nonterminal epoch N -> same state epoch N+1 | authoritative | one per new epoch; repeated/skipped rejects |
| `process_lock_acquired`, `process_lock_released`, `process_lock_crash_reconciled` | run controller for repository/dispatcher acquisition and release; recovery controller for crash reconciliation | acquired authority -> released authority; crash reconciliation is the sole process-death successor | authoritative | a detached pre-flock witness binds the attempt; no authoritative ledger append occurs before the protecting flock is held |
| `run_waiting_on_gate`, `run_active`, `run_resource_blocked`, `run_resource_restored` | product-loop coordinator through dispatcher reducer | `RUNNING <-> WAITING_ON_GATE`; `RUNNING|WAITING_ON_GATE <-> BLOCKED_RESOURCE` with sealed wait/resource evidence | authoritative | identical wait set/resource snapshot no-op; stale restore rejects |
| `run_abort_requested` | CLI authority | nonterminal -> `ABORTING` | authoritative | same reason/authority no-op |
| `run_aborted`, `run_completed`, `run_degraded` | dispatcher reducer; integrity verifier for degraded fact | `ABORTING -> CLOSED/ABORTED`; `ADJUDICATING -> CLOSED/{SHIP,PARTIAL,FAIL}`; any -> `DEGRADED` | authoritative | first terminal fact wins; conflict degrades |
| `pre_execution_adjudication_started` | close-run controller | handled release-blocking pre-execution `RUNNING -> ADJUDICATING` | authoritative | same evidence digest no-op; changed evidence conflicts |
| `phase_started`, `phase_result_committed` | internal phase driver | phase `PENDING -> RUNNING -> terminal` using sealed input digest | authoritative | same digest returns receipt; changed input conflicts |
| `snapshot_written`, `index_rebuilt` | projector | derived watermark advances | authoritative artifact receipt | never changes source truth; head mismatch rejects |
| `capability_pack_sealed`, `research_report_sealed`, `spec_sealed`, `proof_plan_sealed`, `chunk_dag_sealed` | owning phase | absent artifact -> sealed ref | authoritative | ID/hash immutable; changed content new ID |
| `data_policy_bound`, `trust_attestation_bound`, `trust_attestation_revoked` | run controller with operator authority | policy/attestation absent -> bound; current attestation -> revoked | authoritative | digest/authority exact; revocation blocks later execution |
| `redaction_committed`, `disclosure_decided` | data-policy enforcement service | input payload -> redacted/allowed/denied evidence before any remote call | authoritative | exact input+policy digest gives one decision; denial has no call |
| `remote_call_intent`, `remote_call_denied` | research egress controller | classified/redacted/disclosed request -> intent recorded or local policy denial with no effect | authoritative | key binds run/call/attempt, source and effective request hashes, adapter, policy, and precondition; identical duplicate is a no-op and changed digest conflicts |
| `remote_call_committed`, `remote_call_uncertain`, `remote_call_reconciled` | remote-call reconciler | `INTENT_RECORDED -> SUCCESS|ERROR|TIMEOUT|UNCERTAIN`; later uncertainty -> `READY_TO_RETRY|SUCCESS|ERROR|DEGRADED` from sealed observation | authoritative | only exact-ID lookup proves absence; replay-safe reads may allow a fresh attempt without claiming absence; conflicting response/result bytes degrade |
| `chunk_registered` | compiler through dispatcher reducer | absent -> `PENDING` with frozen digest | authoritative | same digest no-op; changed digest degrades |
| `chunk_ready`, `chunk_blocked_by_dep`, `chunk_reopened` | dispatcher reducer | `PENDING -> READY`; dependent -> `BLOCKED_BY_DEP`; cascade-only reopen -> `REPAIRING` | authoritative | legal fold only; repeat no-op |
| `worker_lease_granted`, `worker_lease_expired`, `worker_lease_released` | dispatcher/reaper lease service | `READY -> LEASED`; expiry of unfinished `LEASED|RUNNING` -> `REPAIR_PENDING`; release after `ATTEMPT_FAILED` -> `REPAIR_PENDING`; release after sealed candidate closes worker authority without changing `GATE_PENDING` | authoritative | one live fence and one release; stale fact no state effect |
| `attempt_started`, `attempt_finished`, `attempt_failed` | trusted adapter sidecar | `LEASED -> RUNNING`; completed attempt -> `WORKER_FINISHED`; failed/timed-out/crashed/infra attempt -> `ATTEMPT_FAILED` | authoritative | exact attempt/fence no-op; mismatch conflicts; neither result is proof |
| `candidate_commit_intent`, `candidate_commit_committed` | dispatcher | `WORKER_FINISHED -> GATE_PENDING`; Git intent/action/completion | authoritative | preconditions and completion OID/tree/diff exact |
| `truthful_failure_plant_intent`, `truthful_failure_plant_committed` | trusted failure harness | diagnostic intent -> exact sealed planted preimage/postimage/staged-diff evidence before candidate intent; chunk state unchanged | authoritative | semantic key binds run/chunk/attempt/profile/patch/preimage; exact postimage adopts, mixed or extra paths degrade, and no intent forbids the plant |
| `gate_handoff_committed` | dispatcher gate-lease service | `GATE_PENDING -> GATING`; atomically close worker/open gate lease | authoritative | same handoff no-op; gate fence increments |
| `gate_lease_expired`, `gate_lease_released` | gate reaper | `GATING -> GATE_PENDING`; current lease -> released | authoritative | never returns worker READY; stale no state effect |
| `gate_verdict_committed` | independent gate actor | `GATING -> GATED`; bind the sealed result and close gate authority | authoritative | active commit/fences only; stale never applies |
| `gate_verdict_applied` | dispatcher reducer | `GATED -> MERGE_PENDING|FAILED` from the byte-equal sealed gate-result fold | authoritative | sole later-state owner; identical application is a no-op and changed duplicate conflicts |
| `stale_verdict_discarded` | dispatcher reducer | rejection diagnostic, no state change | authoritative | one per stale verdict ID |
| `merge_plan_intent`, `merge_intent`, `merge_committed`, `merge_conflict` | merge engine holding mutex | diagnostic precompute intent; then `MERGE_PENDING -> MERGED|FAILED` through a sealed `merge_plan.v1` and compare-and-swap ref update | authoritative | key binds plan/prior/candidate/tree/parents/profile/time/ref precondition; exact existing object/ref is idempotent, changed plan or ref conflicts, and no pre-action success exists |
| `provides_satisfied`, `merge_slot_skipped`, `provides_invalidated` | dispatcher reducer | bind unique tokens; advance terminal blocked slot; remove during cascade | authoritative | duplicate provider degrades |
| `cascade_started`, `revert_intent`, `revert_committed`, `cascade_completed` | repair coordinator; merge engine for Git | affected `MERGED -> REPAIRING`, reverse reverts, rebuilt subgraph | authoritative | full plan first; actions idempotent by before/after OID |
| `repair_triggered`, `repair_decision_committed`, `repair_finished` | repair coordinator | `REPAIR_PENDING|FAILED -> REPAIRING`; exact result folds to READY, ABANDONED, or BLOCKED_OPERATOR | authoritative | same trigger+round no-op; one budget decrement; result transition fixed |
| `product_validation_started`, `megatest_result_committed`, `negation_result_committed`, `product_validation_verdict` | independent validator | exact integration tree -> evidence -> `PASS|PARTIAL|FAIL`; authority mismatch emits run-degraded route instead | authoritative | fixed inputs/tree; conflicting verdict degrades |
| `final_adjudication_committed` | pure adjudicator | quiescent trusted evidence -> `SHIP|PARTIAL|FAIL` | authoritative | same evidence same verdict; degraded evidence forbidden |
| `publication_proposed`, `publication_challenge_issued`, `publication_confirmed`, `publication_confirmation_consumed`, `publication_declined` | post-capsule publication planner for proposal/challenge; local operator CLI for confirm/decline; executor for consume | verified capsule + `SHIP` and publication `NONE -> PROPOSED -> CONFIRMED|DECLINED`; consume exactly once before intent | authoritative | digest/nonce/expiry/authority bound; adjudicator cannot emit proposal |
| `publication_intent`, `publication_executed`, `publication_failed`, `publication_collision`, `publication_superseded`, `post_capsule_addendum_committed` | publication executor; planner for supersede/addendum | exact publication schema states; one sealed addendum for every terminal run/publication outcome | authoritative | action follows intent; uncertainty is observe-only; new effect needs fresh confirmation |
| `capsule_finalization_intent`, `capsule_finalized` | capsule finalizer | `OPEN -> FINALIZING -> SEALED`; intent/action/completion | authoritative | same manifest/root/profile; readback before completion |
| `archive_intent`, `archive_committed`, `archive_failed` | archive executor | unarchived -> intent -> verified receipt or fail | authoritative | no-replace; commit after readback |
| `cleanup_plan_committed`, `cleanup_intent`, `cleanup_committed` | cleanup planner/executor with operator authority | dry-run plan -> exact apply -> receipt | authoritative | candidate digest fixed; changed targets skip; no expansion |
| `llm_call_reserved`, `llm_call_committed` | LLM router/budget service | reserve before call; bind immutable record after | authoritative | no double reserve/charge for call/precondition |

Release evidence uses a separate append-only release ledger. These events never enter a run WorkLedger:

| Release event types | Sole legal emitter | Aggregate and legal fold | Durability | Duplicate/reducer rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `release_lock_acquired` | GLOBAL-ACCEPTANCE-08 release runner | no authority -> acquired release authority | authoritative | detached pre-flock witness plus exact path/device/inode, actor/incarnation, ordinal, and precondition; no release-ledger append occurs before flock |
| `release_evidence_intent` | GLOBAL-ACCEPTANCE-08 release runner holding the release lock | acquired authority -> artifact-write authorization binding both terminal run heads and exact output paths | authoritative | same release/input/output digest is a no-op; changed digest conflicts and no path may be replaced |
| `release_evidence_committed` | GLOBAL-ACCEPTANCE-08 release runner holding the release lock | intent -> verified manifest/registry and both release-scoped seal pairs | authoritative | reread must match all sealed hashes; identical completion is a no-op and changed bytes conflict |
| `release_lock_released` | GLOBAL-ACCEPTANCE-08 release runner | acquired authority -> authority closed before OS unlock | authoritative | exact current acquisition only; duplicate is a no-op and stale release has no effect |
| `release_lock_crash_reconciled` | release recovery controller | process-death acquisition -> observed released authority or adopted exact committed evidence | authoritative | sole crash successor; conflicting lock/artifact observation degrades and forbids new effects |

The old `chunk_gate_result`, `merge_started`, `merge_reverted`, `ship_proposed`, and `ship_confirmed` names are removed or read only through a versioned migration adapter; v1 writers emit the taxonomy above. Reducer property tests inject exact duplicates, actor restarts, segment reorder, crash-after-fsync uncertainty, and conflicting idempotency keys and must yield one byte-identical state or explicit `DEGRADED`.

### Genesis, epoch, seal, and capsule schemas

**`run_manifest.v1`**

Producer: `neo run` after source PRD, resolved run config, and schema pack are sealed, before repo preparation, foreground intake, or the first authoritative segment. Consumers: segment genesis, replay, dispatcher, recovery, capsule, integrity/status.

Required fields:

```text
schema_id, schema_version, run_id, created_at, created_by
engine {name="ccc-autocode-neo", version, source_commit:GitOid}
execution_mode: llm_free|live
run_root:RelPath
source_prd:ArtifactRef
run_config:ArtifactRef(run_config.v1)
schema_pack:ArtifactRef
initialization_policy_version:string
```

The genesis digest covers the complete RFC 8785 manifest. It contains no self-hash, epoch/resume/terminal/seal/capsule field and no repo context, enhanced PRD, capability pack, proof plan, research, or other post-genesis output; those are bound later by authoritative sealed-artifact events. `run_root == runs/<run_id>` and the same run ID may never bind a different genesis digest. Reject any post-genesis reference or mutable field.

**`run_epoch_state.v1`**

Producer: dispatcher/recovery reducer. Consumers: segment writer, replay bootstrap, reaper, status. Required fields: `run_id`, `manifest_sha256`, `revision>=0`, `current_epoch>=0`, `previous_epoch>=0|null`, `execution_state:CREATED|PREPARING_REPO|INTAKE_PENDING|INTAKE_ACTIVE|INTAKE_BLOCKED|READY_TO_SUBMIT|SUBMITTING|SUBMISSION_UNCERTAIN|SUBMITTED|RUNNING|WAITING_ON_GATE|BLOCKED_RESOURCE|ADJUDICATING|ABORTING|CLOSED|DEGRADED`, `outcome:null|SHIP|PARTIAL|FAIL|ABORTED|DEGRADED`, `opened_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_at|null`, `opened_by{actor_id,actor_incarnation_id,host_id,pid>=1}`, `resume_event_id|null`, `last_authoritative_event:null|{event_id,epoch,logical_seq,actor_id,actor_incarnation_id,actor_seq}`, and `previous_revision_sha256|null`. Revision 0 uses epoch 0 and null previous/resume/hash. Later epochs increase exactly one, bind a durable resume event in the new epoch, link the prior revision digest, and expire prior-epoch leases before dispatch. `CLOSED` requires a non-null non-degraded outcome and closed time; terminal `DEGRADED` requires outcome DEGRADED and closed time; all other execution states use null outcome and null closed time. Atomic replace occurs only after the corresponding ledger event is durable; reject skipped/repeated epochs or projection/ledger disagreement.

**`artifact_seal.v1`**

Required fields: `seal_id`, `run_id`, `artifact_id`, `artifact_schema_id|null`, `artifact_schema_version>=1|null`, `artifact_path`, `media_type`, `canonicalization:rfc8785|raw_bytes`, `content_sha256`, `content_size_bytes>=0`, `producer_transaction_id`, `authorization_event_id|null`, `sealed_at`, and `sealed_by_actor_id`. Schema ID/version are both null or both present. RFC 8785 requires a JSON media type and schema identity. Raw bytes may be schema-less. Authorization may be null only for pre-ledger genesis inputs; otherwise it is an already durable phase-start/intent/decision event. The later artifact-bound/completion event references this seal, never the reverse. The target is run-relative and immutable; reject mismatched validation, byte count, digest, future-event reference, or undeclared hash projection.

**`capsule_manifest.v1`**

Producer: capsule finalizer after terminal evidence exists. Consumers: offline verifier, archive, audit/report, successor importer. Required fields:

```text
capsule_id, run_id, created_at
capsule_class:VERIFIED_AUDIT|FORENSIC_CAPTURE
terminal_outcome:SHIP|PARTIAL|FAIL|ABORTED|DEGRADED
ledger_integrity {status:VERIFIED|DEGRADED,gaps:[{gap_id,segment_path,
                  byte_offset|null,reason,evidence_ref:ArtifactRef|null}]}
ledger_cutoff_event_id:Id|null
ledger_cutoff_canonical_head_sha256:Sha256|null
genesis_manifest:ArtifactRef(run_manifest.v1)
terminal_epoch_state:ArtifactRef(run_epoch_state.v1)
final_adjudication:ArtifactRef(final_adjudication.v1)|null
postmortem:ArtifactRef(postmortem.v1)
ledger_segments:[{file:FileEntry, actor_id, actor_incarnation_id, epoch,
                  first_seq,last_seq,event_count,terminal_event_hash,
                  chain_status:VERIFIED|BROKEN|TORN_TAIL_DROPPED,
                  torn_tail_dropped}]
snapshots:[FileEntry]
sealed_artifacts:[{artifact:ArtifactRef, seal:ArtifactRef(artifact_seal.v1)}]
blobs:[FileEntry]
git {object_format:sha1|sha256, bundle:FileEntry, base_commit:GitOid,
     integration_commit:GitOid, integration_tree:GitOid,
     included_refs:[{ref:GitRef,oid:GitOid}]}
provenance {run_config,repo_context,proof_plan,requirement_registry:ArtifactRef,
            capability_pack:ArtifactRef|null,prompt_refs:[ArtifactRef],
            llm_call_record_refs:[ArtifactRef],
            tool_records:[{tool_id,version,probe_evidence:ArtifactRef}],
            model_records:[{provider,route_id,requested_model,resolved_model,config_sha256}]}
archive_profile {format="tar.zst",tar_format="pax",path_order="utf8_bytewise",
                 mtime_unix_s=0,uid=0,gid=0,uname="",gname="",
                 file_mode=420,directory_mode=493,symlink_policy="forbid",
                 zstd_level=19,zstd_threads=1,include_detached_capsule_seal=false}
verification_profile:neo_capsule_verify_v1|neo_forensic_capture_verify_v1
evidence_root_sha256
```

The manifest's detached artifact digest covers the full manifest. The evidence root excludes the manifest and detached capsule seal. Sort evidence leaves by UTF-8 path; leaf `SHA256(0x00 || UTF8(path) || 0x00 || raw_sha256_bytes)`; parent `SHA256(0x01 || left || right)`; duplicate the last node at an odd level; empty trees are forbidden. The Git bundle must reconstruct base/integration objects and tree offline, with the integration ref at the integration commit. `VERIFIED_AUDIT` requires VERIFIED ledger integrity, no broken segment, non-null cutoff fields, the normal verification profile, and exact chain verification from genesis through the cutoff. SHIP/PARTIAL/FAIL require a matching final adjudication; ABORTED requires null adjudication. `FORENSIC_CAPTURE` is mandatory for DEGRADED, requires at least one integrity gap or broken segment, null final adjudication, the forensic profile, and never authorizes adjudication, publication, or cleanup; nullable cutoff fields name the last verified event/head when one exists. Live verified capsules include a capability pack; LLM-free capsules may use null. The postmortem outcome and integrity match the manifest. Final adjudication and postmortem contain no capsule/archive hash. The capsule closes autonomous build evidence before operator-controlled publication; later publication events never rewrite it.

**Detached `capsule_seal.v1`**

Required fields: `seal_id`, `capsule_id`, `run_id`, `capsule_class:VERIFIED_AUDIT|FORENSIC_CAPTURE`, `capsule_manifest_sha256`, `evidence_root_sha256`, `archive_format="tar.zst"`, `canonical_tar_sha256`, `canonical_tar_size_bytes>=1`, `archive_path`, `archive_sha256`, `archive_size_bytes>=1`, `finalization_transaction_id`, `finalization_intent_event_id`, `sealed_at`, `sealed_by_actor_id`, and `verification_profile:neo_capsule_verify_v1|neo_forensic_capture_verify_v1`. Class/profile must match the manifest. It is physically excluded from both tar and archive. Full reread must prove archive bytes, decompressed canonical tar bytes, manifest bytes, evidence root, and canonical metadata before `capsule_finalized` binds this seal; reject early hashing, a future completion-event reference, inclusion of the seal, or any mismatch. A forensic seal proves captured bytes, not ledger truth, and is never publication- or cleanup-eligible.

### Planning, runtime-evidence, and proof schemas

The following immutable artifacts all use the shared identity fields and detached seals. Refreshes create new artifact IDs and use an optional `supersedes_ref`; no schema contains `content_sha256`.

**`repo_context.v1`**

Required body:

```text
repo_identity {kind:greenfield|adopted, common_dir_realpath:AbsPath,
               common_dir_key_sha256:Sha256, operator_worktree_realpath:AbsPath|null}
base {ref:string, commit_oid:GitOid, tree_oid:GitOid}
run_integration {worktree_realpath:AbsPath, branch:GitRef}
lock {mode="exclusive_full_run", key_sha256:Sha256, acquired_event_id:Id}
git_inventory {submodules:[{path:RelPath,commit_oid:GitOid}],
               lfs{enabled,pointers_resolved},
               sparse_checkout{enabled,patterns_sha256|null},
               worktrees_ref,hooks_ref,filters_ref:ArtifactRef}
maps {path_inventory_ref,dependency_map_ref,interface_map_ref:ArtifactRef}
boundaries {allowed_paths:[string],protected_paths:[string]}
dirty_state {mode:clean|preserved_dirty,status_sha256:Sha256,
             baseline_diff_ref:ArtifactRef|null,dirty_paths:[RelPath]}
drift_sha256:Sha256
```

Clean mode requires null baseline diff and no dirty paths. `preserved_dirty` requires a sealed baseline diff; every dirty path is protected from neo writes unless one approved task explicitly owns that path and records before/after proof. The current target scaffold uses clean adoption at commit `ad9c9a1d367e558d338e7bc78c836bdad0cc54f6`, tree `4c674a3d978b993349b81d466876e47af3797fc0`; generated roots remain protected and any later dirt or identity drift blocks preflight. Operator and integration worktrees differ; integration branch matches the run; lock key equals common-dir identity; allowed/protected sets are disjoint; hooks/filters are recorded but not executed during discovery. Reject unsealed dirt, operator-checkout repinning, unauthorized dirty-path overlap, or stale drift hash.

**`proof_plan.v1`**

Required body: `requirements:[{requirement_id,criticality:release_required|optional,statement_sha256,proofs:[{proof_id,oracle_type:registry_baseline|external_oracle|property|integration|smoke|analysis,oracle_ref:ArtifactRef,provenance:registry_pinned|external_blessed|operator_approved,independence:gate_owned|external,visibility:gate_only|worker_visible_contract,counts_toward_verdict:boolean,command{argv:[string],cwd="clean_copy"},environment_profile_ref:ArtifactRef(sanitized_git_profile.v1),tool_manifest_ref:ArtifactRef(compatibility_manifest.v1),expected_exit_codes:[0..125],timeout_s:1..3600,fallback:block|ask_ryan|defer_optional,negative_control_ref:ArtifactRef}]}]`, `unmapped_required_ids:[Id]`, and `coverage_sha256`. Before sealing, every release-required requirement has an admissible proof, unmapped required IDs are empty, `defer_optional` is not used for required scope, every proof has a negative control, every environment/tool ref resolves to sealed builder-accessible bytes, each proof timeout is at most 3600 seconds, the sum of timeout seconds for one chunk is at most 7200, and gate-only oracle refs cannot enter worker context. Reject proofless required criteria or worker-visible hidden oracles.

**`capability_pack.v1`**

Required body: `compatibility_manifest_ref:ArtifactRef(compatibility_manifest.v1)`, `host{identity_sha256,os,arch}`, `observed_at`, `expires_at`, `entries:[{capability_id,required_for:[research|synthesis|worker|gate|review|publication],owner,probe{kind:command|http,argv|null,url|null,method:GET|null,timeout_s:1..120},expected{exit_codes:[integer],status_codes:[100..599],media_type|null,schema_ref|null,content_predicate|null,version_policy,allowed_versions},observed{started_at,duration_ms,status_code|null,exit_code|null,media_type|null,version|null,schema_valid|null,content_match|null,evidence_ref},result:pass|fail|degraded,failure_policy:fail|degrade,failure_class:unavailable|timeout|incompatible_version|invalid_schema|deceptive_content|stale_evidence|null}]`, and `pack_status:pass|degraded|fail`. Exactly one argv/URL is present. Expected policy/versions/features equal the sealed compatibility manifest. Required failure folds pack to fail. HTTP reachability alone never passes. Expiry is derived from immutable observation.

**`compatibility_manifest.v1`**

Required fields are manifest ID/time, creator, and sorted unique entries `[{component_id,kind:CLI|PYTHON_PACKAGE|HTTP_SERVICE,required_for,version_policy:EXACT|RANGE|OPERATOR_PINNED_EXACT|FEATURE_ONLY,allowed_versions,required_features:[{feature_id,probe_kind:COMMAND|HTTP,argv:null|[string],url:null|string,expected_exit_codes,expected_status_codes,content_predicate,schema_ref:null|ArtifactRef}],use_mode:EXTERNAL_PROCESS|PYTHON_DEPENDENCY|REMOTE_SERVICE,source_evidence_refs,operator_authority_ref:null|ArtifactRef}]`. EXACT has one allowed version; RANGE has one PEP-440/semver constraint selected by component type; OPERATOR_PINNED_EXACT has one operator-authorized exact version and non-null authority; FEATURE_ONLY has an empty allowed list but still records the observed version and requires every feature probe. Command versus HTTP fields are exclusive. A new version is a new manifest revision and must pass the same component integration selector before adoption.

The initial build baseline is literal: Dagu CLI `2.7.16` EXACT as an external process with `version`, `validate`, `start`, and `schema dag handler_on` proving an always-run `handler_on.exit`; Ralph CLI `2.8.1` EXACT with attach/model/directory feature probes; CPython RANGE `>=3.12,<3.13`; `uv` CLI `0.11.16` EXACT; Git CLI `2.50.1` EXACT; zstd CLI `1.5.7` EXACT for canonical compression; and Python package `jsonschema==4.26.0`. OpenCode slots use OPERATOR_PINNED_EXACT because the binary is not on this host PATH; each live slot must supply its exact approved version plus machine-readable version, attach, and content-valid health probes. OmniRoute and oMLX are FEATURE_ONLY remote services with version recorded and schema/content probes; raw port/HTTP success is insufficient. The capability pack may not silently widen any baseline.

**`proof_kernel_source_binding.v1`**

Producer: `NEO-M0-005` preflight before any transplant write. Consumers: transplant copier, schema/proof tests, capsule, cold-builder handoff. Closed and immutable. Required fields: `binding_id`, source repository absolute path, `commit_oid="91d7db126380265f9161c88efe72e6a307f859be"`, `root_tree_oid="ad77b6c52be4033e2bccaa95eb53afa69b724e16"`, `object_read_mode="GIT_OBJECT_DATABASE"`, `working_tree_used=false`, sorted required entries `[{path,kind:BLOB|TREE,git_oid,sha256:null|Sha256}]`, extraction argv arrays, target mapping `[{source_path,target_path,target_sha256}]`, Git executable path/hash/version, verification time, verifier actor, and `status="VERIFIED"`. Blob rows require SHA-256; tree rows require null SHA-256 and their literal Git tree OID. The required entries, every blob and tree object identity, the 33 exact `git cat-file blob` argv arrays, the source-to-target mappings, and the canonical target tree-manifest digests equal the builder-accessible immutable binding `/Users/ryanpappal/01_VAULT/KnR-Vault/00_MAIN/01_ActiveProjects/ccc-autocode-neo/prd-v0.3.0/iterations/260712-b-loop-r2a/R2A-REPAIR-BUILDER-BINDING-AUTOCODE-LITE-r001.json`, SHA-256 `00607f983b56f78e2f670a3da3d92dd62e10e5a12041f97b8d6143edf2880f67`; no inherited plan or unavailable closure layer is needed. The producer verifies each object with `git cat-file`, rejects symlink/gitlink types, streams blob bytes from the named commit, and never reads the checkout file. Missing object, branch-only resolution, dirty-byte substitution, unexpected path, or any hash mismatch blocks before target creation. Same inputs reproduce byte-identical binding bytes; changing `main` has no effect.

**`sanitized_git_profile.v1`**

Producer: repository preflight. Consumers: every Git subprocess, proof gate, merge engine, publication planner, acceptance. Closed and immutable. Required fields: `profile_id`, Git executable absolute path/SHA-256/version, `config_mode="ISOLATED"`, empty sealed HOME and XDG config roots, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1"`, sorted allowed environment keys, sorted required `-c key=value` arguments, hook directory ref/hash, attributes policy, filters policy, credential policy, signing policy, protocol policy, submodule/LFS policy, probe argv/result/evidence refs, created time, and verifier actor. It also requires `commit_identity{name="ccc-autocode-neo",email="ccc-autocode-neo@invalid",timezone="+0000"}`; no runtime, repository, operator, or environment override exists. v1 requires an empty sealed hooks directory, `core.attributesFile=/dev/null`, no `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`, no external diff or merge driver, no credential helper or askpass, no signing program, no repository config include, no clean/smudge/process filter, no submodule, and no LFS pointer. Network protocols are denied for build/gate/merge and enabled only by the separately authorized publication transaction. Every Git call uses the sealed executable plus the complete sealed argument prefix and environment allowlist. An injected system/global/local config, include, hook, filter, helper, askpass, executable, attributes file, or environment variable must fail its targeted negative fixture.

**`worker_slot_capability.v1`**

Required fields: `slot_id`, `url`, `config_path:AbsPath`, `config_sha256`, `pinned_routes:[string]`, `version`, `probes{health_entry_id,attach_entry_id,version_entry_id}`, `verified_at`, `expires_at`, `status:healthy|unhealthy|draining`, `capacity{max_active_workers=1}`, `ownership="shared_operator"`, `mutation_policy="no_restart_no_reconfigure"`, and `evidence_refs:[ArtifactRef]`. Healthy requires all three probes; mutable `combo/*` routes are forbidden on gate-owned paths; neo never restarts or rewrites a slot.

**`worker_context_pack.v1`**

Required fields: `chunk_id`, `attempt_id`, `lease_id`, `candidate_fence>=1`, `chunk_spec_ref`, `spec_slice_ref`, `repo_context_ref`, `provider_interface_refs`, `research_finding_refs`, `prior_failure_packet_refs`, `required_outputs`, `acceptance_statements:[{requirement_id,statement}]`, `allowed_paths`, `must_not_touch`, `guardrail_ref`, `neutralization{version,applied_to:[research|prior_failures|provider_interfaces]}`, `rendered_prompt_ref`, `rendered_prompt_sha256`, `allowed_env_keys`, and `excluded_classes`. `excluded_classes` must contain `proof_oracle`, `hidden_baseline`, `registry_path`, `raw_research`, `provider_secret`, and `other_chunk_spec`; no such reference may appear anywhere. Fence/lease and boundaries equal the sealed chunk; all untrusted reused text is neutralized.

**`failure_packet.v1`**

Required fields: `failure_id`, `scope:attempt|chunk|gate|merge|phase|product|publication`, `phase`, `chunk_id|null`, `attempt_id|null`, `failure_class:timeout|infra|proof|path_policy|merge_conflict|budget|capability|integrity|config|publication|unknown`, `criticality:release_blocking|optional`, `trigger_event_id`, `summary` 1–4096 chars, nonempty `evidence_refs`, `failing_proof_ids`, `missing_outputs`, `retryable`, `retry_after_s|null`, `fence|null`, `budget{repair_generation>=0,max_attempts_per_generation>=1,attempts_remaining,chunk_repairs_remaining,product_rounds_remaining}`, `recommended_action:retry|reroute|repair|abort|operator_review`, `must_not_touch`, and `lesson`. Attempt scope requires chunk/attempt/fence. Non-retryable uses null delay. Lessons remain untrusted and are neutralized before worker reuse.

**Execution, gate, repair, validation, and adjudication evidence**

`lease_liveness_observation.v1` is a disposable sidechannel record, not an artifact and not a WorkLedger event. The trusted sidecar atomically replaces `runs/<run_id>/liveness/<lease_id>.json` with a closed record containing lease/run/chunk/attempt IDs, epoch, candidate and authority fences, owner incarnation, monotonically increasing observation sequence, observed monotonic and wall times, resource health, and a checksum. It is excluded from manifests, seals, segments, snapshots, indexes, canonical heads, replay, capsules, archives, and acceptance proof. The reaper may read it only to decide whether to append one authoritative `worker_lease_expired` or `gate_lease_expired` event. That expiry event embeds the sampled sequence/times/fences and deadline; later absence of the disposable observation does not change replay. Malformed, stale, mismatched, or missing observations never renew a lease.

`lease.v1` is an immutable grant, not mutable lease state. Required fields are `lease_id`, `run_id`, `chunk_id`, `attempt_id`, `kind:WORKER|GATE`, `owner_actor_id`, `owner_incarnation_id`, `resource_id`, `epoch>=0`, `candidate_fence>=1`, `authority_fence>=1`, `previous_authority_fence>=1|null`, `previous_lease_id|null`, `worktree_id|null`, `candidate_commit_oid:null|GitOid`, `candidate_tree_oid:null|GitOid`, `gate_request_ref:null|ArtifactRef`, `heartbeat_source:ADAPTER_SIDECAR|GATE_RUNNER`, `heartbeat_interval_ms>=100`, `ttl_ms>=1000`, `grant_transaction_id`, `granted_at`, and `initial_state="ACTIVE"`. `ttl_ms >= 3 * heartbeat_interval_ms`. A worker grant has `authority_fence=candidate_fence`, non-null worktree, null candidate OIDs/request, and adapter heartbeat. A gate grant has null worktree, non-null candidate OIDs/request, and gate-runner heartbeat. Null previous fence requires authority fence 1; otherwise the new fence is previous+1 and the prior lease ID is non-null. The grant event references this already sealed artifact; the artifact never contains its future grant-event ID. `ACTIVE|EXPIRED|RELEASED` and heartbeat liveness are event-derived only.

`attempt.v1` is the trusted adapter/supervisor's immutable finished-attempt record. Required fields are `attempt_id`, `run_id`, `chunk_id`, `iteration>=1`, `worker_lease_ref:ArtifactRef(lease.v1)`, `candidate_fence>=1`, worker actor/incarnation, slot/adapter IDs and adapter version, `driver{kind:LLM|DETERMINISTIC_FIXTURE,model_route:null|{provider,requested_model,resolved_model,config_sha256},fixture_id:null|Id}`, context-pack ref, worktree ID/base OID, allowed-paths hash, `start_transaction_id`, `finish_transaction_id`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `termination:COMPLETED|FAILED|TIMED_OUT|CRASHED|INFRA_ERROR`, nullable process exit/signal, worker-reported outcome `SUCCESS|FAILURE|UNKNOWN`, worker-result ref, nullable output-tree OID/stdout/stderr refs, duration, nullable failure class `SPEC|IMPLEMENTATION|INFRA|TIMEOUT|BOUNDARY|UNKNOWN`, nullable lesson ref, and budget `{timeout_ms>=1,retry_ordinal>=0,model_spend_usd:Usd|null}`. LLM requires a model route and null fixture; deterministic fixture requires a fixture and null route/spend. Completion requires exit 0, no signal, output tree, and null failure; timeout requires failure class TIMEOUT. Nullable ref pairs are structurally coupled. Worker narration is telemetry only; gate verdict and merge eligibility fields are forbidden. The record is sealed/fsynced before `attempt_finished`, which references it; it contains no future finish-event ID.

`gate_request.v1` is produced and sealed by the dispatcher after `candidate_commit_committed` and before the gate lease is granted. Consumers are the gate runner, proof-result aggregator, verdict reducer, merge preflight, and capsule. It is a closed immutable Draft 2020-12 object with required fields: `request_id`, `run_id`, `chunk_id`, `attempt_id`, `candidate_fence>=1`, `requested_gate_fence>=1`, `candidate_commit_event_id`, `candidate_commit_oid`, `candidate_tree_oid`, `source_lock{source_prd_sha256,target_scaffold_base_commit_oid,repo_context_ref,repo_context_sha256,proof_kernel_source_binding_ref,proof_kernel_source_binding_sha256}`, `schema_pack_ref`, `proof_plan_ref`, `requirement_registry_ref`, `sanitized_git_profile_ref`, `clean_copy_profile{archive_format="git_bundle",checkout_mode="DETACHED",submodules=false,lfs=false,network=false}`, sorted `proofs:[{proof_id,requirement_id,oracle_ref,negative_control_ref,argv:[string],cwd="CLEAN_COPY_ROOT",environment_profile_ref,tool_manifest_ref,expected_exit_codes:[integer],timeout_s:1..3600,counts_toward_verdict:boolean}]`, `path_policy{allowed_paths,must_not_touch,required_outputs}`, `input_digest`, `created_at`, and `created_by`. It contains no gate lease ref, verdict ref, result ref, future event ID, or self-hash; only its detached seal is excluded from its content hash.

The request contains the complete sorted 1..64-row chunk union, at least one row counts toward the verdict, and the timeout sum is at most 7200 seconds. Every row, including `counts_toward_verdict`, byte-equals its sealed proof-plan row. The request ID is `"gate-request-"+SHA256(RFC8785(all fields except request_id,created_at))`. `input_digest` is SHA-256 over the ordered content hashes of the candidate commit/tree, source lock, schema pack, proof plan, requirement registry, sanitized Git profile, clean-copy profile, proof rows, and path policy. Proof rows equal exactly the release-required proof-plan rows for the chunk and preserve their argv, expected exits, oracle, negative control, tools, and timeouts byte-for-byte. The dispatcher seals the request, then creates a gate `lease.v1` that references it, then commits one `gate_handoff_committed` event binding both artifacts; this order prevents a hash cycle. A crash before handoff leaves no active gate. A crash after handoff reuses the same sealed request and lease. Any input drift creates a different request and requires a new gate fence. Positive fixtures cover one valid request and idempotent recovery. Negative fixtures independently change the candidate tree, proof-plan hash, registry hash, argv, environment, tool hash, oracle, negative control, allowed path, output, and source lock and must reject before proof execution.

`proof_result.v1` is emitted only by the independent gate actor. Required fields are proof-result/run/chunk/attempt/gate-request/gate-lease IDs, gate and candidate fences, candidate commit/tree OIDs, proof ID/type `ACCEPTANCE|REGRESSION|PROPERTY|GOLDEN|INTEGRATION|SMOKE|ANALYSIS`, nonempty exact command argv, `working_scope="CLEAN_COPY_ROOT"`, `oracle{kind:REGISTRY_PINNED|EXTERNAL_BLESSED|COMMAND_EXIT|NONE_ADVISORY,ref:ArtifactRef|null,authority_ref:ArtifactRef|null}`, `counts_toward_verdict`, timeout, start/complete/duration, nullable exit code, timeout flag, oracle evaluation `MATCH|MISMATCH|NOT_APPLICABLE|ERROR`, `passed`, nullable stdout/stderr refs, observed artifact refs, clean-copy hash, and gate-engine version. Passing requires no timeout, exit 0, and oracle MATCH or NOT_APPLICABLE. Verdict-counting proof may not use NONE_ADVISORY; registry/external oracle requires both refs; NONE_ADVISORY requires both null and cannot count. Proof identity, command, oracle, and expected exit must equal the sealed proof plan. An advisory result can never satisfy a required proof.

`gate_result.v1` is the gate actor's immutable aggregate. Required fields are gate-result/run/chunk/attempt/gate-request IDs, gate-request ref, gate-lease ref, gate actor, gate and candidate fences, candidate commit/tree OIDs, proof-plan and requirement-registry refs, clean-copy hash, `candidate_verified_at_start`, `candidate_verified_at_end`, proof-result refs, `proof_summary{total,verdict_counting_passed,verdict_counting_failed,verdict_counting_timed_out,advisory_passed,advisory_failed,advisory_timed_out}`, `path_policy{passed,diff_sha256,violations}`, `output_policy{passed,missing_outputs}`, verdict `PASS|FAIL|NEEDS_PROOF_SPEC`, unique failure codes from `PROOF_FAILED|PROOF_TIMEOUT|PROOF_TAMPERED|PATH_VIOLATION|MISSING_OUTPUT|NEEDS_PROOF_SPEC|CANDIDATE_CHANGED`, start/complete/duration, gate-engine version, and the prior `gate_handoff_event_id`. Summary categories are mutually exclusive and fold exactly over referenced proof results. PASS requires both candidate verifications, path/output pass, zero verdict-counting failure/timeout, and every verdict-counting proof pass; advisory results remain visible but never control the verdict. NEEDS_PROOF_SPEC is legal only when a required proof lacks an admissible gate-owned oracle and carries its matching code. Every other non-PASS result is FAIL with at least one matching failure code. `gate_verdict_committed` references this already sealed artifact; the artifact contains no forward verdict-event ID.

`validation_report.v1` is the independent product validator's immutable result for one integration tree. Required fields are validation/run IDs, `validation_round>=0`, integration commit/tree OIDs, spec and requirement-registry refs, input ledger head and projected-index head hashes, `index_state:FRESH|STALE|DEGRADED`, replay-clean boolean, required/optional requirement ID sets, integration-proof refs, `megatest{mode:LLM_FREE|LIVE,fixture_id,fixture_version,passed,proof_refs}`, `negation{confirmed,planted:[{defect_id,injection_ref,detected,proof_ref}]}`, advisory AI review with nullable findings ref, `scope_summary{required_total,required_passed,optional_total,optional_passed}`, failing requirement IDs, verdict `PASS|PARTIAL|FAIL|DEGRADED`, `validation_transaction_id`, and start/complete/duration. Counts fold exactly; every failing ID is declared; AI review cannot alter verdict. PASS requires FRESH/equal heads, clean replay, megatest pass, negation confirmed with every planted defect detected, all required and optional proof pass, and no failing ID. PARTIAL requires the same authority/megatest/negation conditions, all required proof pass, and at least one optional failure. FAIL requires FRESH/equal heads and clean replay plus a required-proof, megatest, or negation failure. DEGRADED is mandatory for unequal heads, degraded index, or unclean replay and cannot be adjudicated. The report contains no future validation-verdict event ID; `product_validation_verdict` binds it after sealing.

`repair_decision.v1` is the repair coordinator's immutable one-trigger decision. Required fields are repair/run IDs, decision sequence, trigger event/type `CHUNK_FAIL|PRODUCT_FAIL|MERGE_CONFLICT|GATE_INFRA_EXHAUSTED`, `tier:1|2|3|4`, nonempty affected chunk IDs and trigger evidence, failure class `IMPLEMENTATION|PROOF|BOUNDARY|MERGE|REGRESSION|INFRA|TIMEOUT|RESOURCE|UNKNOWN`, action `RETRY_SAME|RETRY_REROUTED|REPAIR_CHUNK|CASCADE_REOPEN|ABANDON|ESCALATE_OPERATOR`, `repair_scope{allowed_paths,must_not_touch,spec_slice_refs}`, run-config ref, budget-policy hash, before/after snapshots `{repair_generation>=0,max_attempts_per_generation>=1,attempts_remaining,chunk_repairs_remaining,product_rounds_remaining,wallclock_remaining_ms,model_spend_remaining_usd:Usd|null}`, nullable model route, nullable cascade plan `[{chunk_id,merge_commit_oid}]`, required proof IDs, rationale ref, deciding actor, and time. Wall-clock, spend, product-round, and chunk-repair budgets never increase. Tier 1 is RETRY_SAME, requires at least one attempt before, keeps repair_generation fixed, and decrements attempts exactly once. Tier 2 begins only after attempts reach zero, is RETRY_REROUTED or REPAIR_CHUNK, requires a nonempty scoped repair and proof set, requires one chunk-repair credit, decrements that credit exactly once, increments repair_generation exactly one, keeps max_attempts_per_generation equal to the sealed run-config value, and resets attempts_remaining exactly to max_attempts_per_generation for the new generation; this paired reset is the sole legal increasing budget field. Reroute also requires a model route. Tier 3 is CASCADE_REOPEN after PRODUCT_FAIL, requires one product-round credit and a complete reverse-merge-order plan containing the selected merged chunks plus every already-merged transitive dependent, then decrements the product round exactly once. Tier 4 is ABANDON or ESCALATE_OPERATOR, opens no attempt, consumes no new repair credit, and operator escalation performs no automatic repository mutation. Wall-clock and spend can only decrease. The decision cannot itself mutate Git or state; the durable decision event authorizes later exact actions.

`final_adjudication.v1` is emitted only by the pure adjudicator over a quiescent, trustworthy evidence cut. Required fields are adjudication/run IDs, `adjudication_scope:PRE_EXECUTION|PRODUCT`, `input_execution_state="ADJUDICATING"`, policy ID/version/hash, run-manifest ref, input ledger-head event/hash, equal projected-index head hash, replay-proof ref with `replay_clean=true`, chunk outcomes `[{chunk_id,criticality:RELEASE_REQUIRED|OPTIONAL,terminal_state:MERGED|ABANDONED|BLOCKED_BY_DEP,gate_result_ref:ArtifactRef|null}]`, nullable validation-report ref and nullable validation verdict `PASS|PARTIAL|FAIL`, negation-confirmed boolean, required/optional total/merged counts, abandoned and blocked chunk IDs, `ship_conditions{all_release_required_merged,all_optional_merged,product_validation_passed,negation_confirmed,ledger_replay_clean,evidence_complete}`, verdict `SHIP|PARTIAL|FAIL`, publication-eligible boolean, rationale codes drawn from `ALL_SCOPE_VERIFIED|OPTIONAL_SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE|REQUIRED_SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE|VALIDATION_FAILED|NEGATION_FAILED|EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE|PREFLIGHT_FAILED|RESEARCH_BLOCKED|PROOF_PLAN_BLOCKED|SYNTHESIS_FAILED|DAG_INVALID`, `input_evidence_root_sha256`, adjudicator, and time. Counts fold exactly; each merged chunk has a matching PASS gate result. PRODUCT requires a non-null validation report/verdict. SHIP requires PRODUCT, every condition true, every chunk merged, empty abandoned/blocked sets, validation PASS, and publication eligibility true. PARTIAL requires PRODUCT, all release-required chunks merged, trustworthy complete evidence, validation PARTIAL caused only by optional unavailable scope, at least one unavailable optional chunk, and publication eligibility false. PRODUCT FAIL covers unavailable required chunks, validation FAIL, failed negation, or a known missing required proof with otherwise trustworthy replay. PRE_EXECUTION requires empty chunk/abandon/block sets, zero counts, null validation, false negation/ship conditions except clean replay and evidence completeness, verdict FAIL, publication eligibility false, and exactly one matching pre-execution rationale code plus optional EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE. No artifact is produced for ABORTED, DEGRADED, stale index, broken replay, or validation DEGRADED. The input evidence root covers the ordered detached evidence refs and excludes this artifact. Capsule, archive, publication proposal, and future terminal-event references are forbidden.

`postmortem.v1` is the immutable run closeout analysis. Required fields are postmortem/run IDs, outcome `SHIP|PARTIAL|FAIL|ABORTED|DEGRADED`, run-manifest ref, observed ledger-head hash, `close_transaction_id`, `terminal_trigger_event_id`, `ledger_integrity:VERIFIED|DEGRADED`, nullable final-adjudication ref, phase summaries `[{phase_id,outcome:PASS|FAIL|ABORTED|DEGRADED|SKIPPED|NEEDS_CLARIFICATION,duration_ms,evidence_refs}]`, chunk summaries `[{chunk_id,criticality,terminal_state:MERGED|ABANDONED|BLOCKED_BY_DEP|CANCELLED_BY_RUN,attempts,total_duration_ms,final_gate_result_ref:null|ArtifactRef}]`, failure-class set, root causes with nonempty evidence, repair-decision refs, evidence gaps, `cost{completeness:COMPLETE|PARTIAL|UNAVAILABLE,known_total_usd:Usd|null,unknown_cost_call_ids}`, wall time, lessons `[{lesson_id,text_ref}]`, body ref, creator, and time. SHIP/PARTIAL/FAIL require VERIFIED integrity and a matching final adjudication; ABORTED/DEGRADED require null adjudication, and DEGRADED requires degraded integrity. FAIL, ABORTED, or DEGRADED requires a failure class, root cause, or explicit evidence gap. Complete cost has a total and no unknown calls; partial has at least one unknown call; unavailable has null total. SHIP contains no abandoned or blocked chunk. The terminal run event references this already sealed record by the same close transaction; the postmortem never embeds that future event ID. Lessons and body are untrusted text, are never automatic memory writes, and are neutralized before reuse. Inline secret/file bodies, capsule hashes, and future archive/publication references are forbidden.

**`phase_result.v1`**

Required fields: `phase_result_id`, `phase:capability_preflight|research|proof_plan|synthesize_spec|compile_chunk_dag|execute_product_loop|close_run|seal_capsule`, `invocation_id`, `epoch>=0`, `input_refs`, `input_digest`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `status:SUCCEEDED|FAILED_HANDLED|ABORTED_HANDLED|DEGRADED_HANDLED|SKIPPED|RETRYABLE_ERROR`, `internal_process_exit_code`, `domain_exit_code`, `output_refs`, `first_owned_event_id|null`, `last_owned_event_id_before_receipt|null`, `metrics{wall_time_ms,llm_calls,cost_usd:Usd|null,cost_mode:exact|bounded|disabled}`, `failure_packet_ref|null`, `next_phase:null|capability_preflight|research|proof_plan|synthesize_spec|compile_chunk_dag|execute_product_loop|close_run|seal_capsule`, and `idempotency_digest`. The event range contains only already durable phase-owned events and never the future `phase_result_committed` event that binds this receipt. The research phase emits both report and research-quality artifacts; optional-only quality degradation remains SUCCEEDED with output quality DEGRADED. A sealed SUCCEEDED, FAILED_HANDLED, ABORTED_HANDLED, DEGRADED_HANDLED, or SKIPPED receipt uses internal process exit 0; the domain exit records the truthful eventual operator outcome. Only RETRYABLE_ERROR uses a nonzero internal exit and Dagu retry. Business success advances to the next business phase; any handled terminal route names `close_run`; `close_run` names `seal_capsule`; seal success names null. Dagu's always-run exit finalizer reads this sealed next-phase intent and invokes close/seal only for a handled terminal route or completed business graph; a transport crash cannot advance. `close_run` emits pre-execution or product adjudication when evidence is trustworthy, emits postmortem for every terminal route, and omits adjudication for abort/degraded. Retry exhaustion without a handled receipt leaves the run nonterminal/resumable rather than falsely closed. The same idempotency digest reproduces the byte-identical result.

**`llm_call_record.v1`**

Required fields: `call_id`, `phase`, `lane:intake|research|synthesis|worker|rescue|ai_review`, `chunk_id|null`, `attempt_id|null`, `provider`, `requested_model`, `resolved_model`, `route_id`, `request_ref`, `request_sha256`, `response_ref|null`, `response_sha256|null`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `status:success|error|timeout|cancelled`, `timeout_s`, `usage{input_tokens|null,output_tokens|null,cached_input_tokens|null,tool_calls}`, `accounting{mode:exact|bounded|disabled,currency="USD",reserved_usd|null,actual_usd|null}`, `data_policy_ref`, `disclosure_ref|null`, `redaction_ref|null`, and `error_class|null`. Success requires response and no error. Enabled cap forbids disabled accounting. Exact requires actual cost; bounded requires reservation. Worker lane requires chunk/attempt. Credentials never appear.

**`research_quality.v1`**

Required fields: `research_plan_ref`, `research_report_ref`, `questions:[{question_id,criticality:required|optional,evidence_predicate:primary_source|official_source|empirical_probe|approved_reasoned_analysis,minimum_evidence_count>=1,verified_finding_ids,lead_finding_ids,result:satisfied|unsatisfied|unavailable}]`, `coverage{required_total,required_covered,required_ratio,optional_total,optional_covered,optional_ratio}`, `source_counts{primary,secondary,leads}`, `outage_failure_refs`, `status:PASS|DEGRADED|BLOCKED`, `continue_to_synthesis`, `reasons`, and `evaluated_at`. Counts/ratios equal rows; zero denominator is `1.0`; continuation requires required ratio 1.0; PASS requires all questions satisfied; DEGRADED permits only optional gaps/outages; any required gap is BLOCKED.

**`requirement_registry.v1` and `acceptance_proof.v1`**

Registry required fields: `source_identity{kind="FILE_SHA256",path:AbsPath,sha256:Sha256}`, `target_scaffold_base_commit_oid:GitOid`, `proof_kernel_source_binding_ref:ArtifactRef(proof_kernel_source_binding.v1)`, `requirements:[{requirement_id,kind:task|global_acceptance,statement,owner_task_ids,depends_on_requirement_ids,consumes_artifact_ids,produces_artifact_ids,test_module,test_selector,command_argv,cwd:AbsPath,environment_profile_ref:ArtifactRef,config_ref:ArtifactRef,timeout_s:1..7200,expected_exit,proof_path_template,positive_oracle{schema_id="acceptance_proof.v1",artifact_ids,expected_verdict="PASS"},negative_control_bundle{bundle_id,executor_argv,controls:[{control_id,stimulus_contract,stimulus_sha256,expected_rejection}],completion_predicate},authority_class:static_prd|calibrated|operator_policy}]`, and `external_inputs:[{artifact_id,path,identity_kind:FILE_SHA256|GIT_COMMIT_TREE|GIT_BLOB|GIT_TREE,sha256:null|Sha256,git_oid:null|GitOid,authority_ref}]`. `acceptance_proof.v1` requires requirement/registry/source/lock hashes, exact argv, actual/expected exit, stdout/stderr refs and hashes, negative-control result, produced artifact IDs/paths/hashes, gate actor/fence/event, start/end times, and verdict. Task-kind registry rows require timeout_s<=3600; global-acceptance rows may use timeout_s<=7200 and never enter a chunk gate request.  Task and global source rows retain ordered `required_negative_controls` strings. The compiler expands each string `s` at zero-based ordinal `i` into `control_id="NC-"+requirement_id+"-"+two_digit(i+1)+"-"+first12(SHA256(UTF8(s)))`; `bundle_id="NCB-"+requirement_id+"-"+first16(SHA256(RFC8785(control_objects)))`. The row's primary acceptance selector executes the exact set. Each result binds the control ID, stimulus string/hash, witness selector, observed product code/detail when named, inner predicate REJECTED, and outer verifier exit 0. Bundle PASS requires exact set equality and every inner rejection; otherwise the requirement fails. Registry rows are sorted by ID; every producer is unique; all consumers resolve; the dependency graph is acyclic; proof paths/selectors are unique; every task reaches a global criterion; worker/self-authored reports never satisfy proof.

**`resource_calibration.v1`**

Required fields: `host_identity_sha256`, `physical_ram_bytes`, `sample_policy{deterministic_serial_samples>=10,live_samples_per_route>=0}`, `selected_routes`, measurements for `worker_rss_p95`, `gate_rss_p95`, `dispatcher_rss_p95`, `inference_rss`, `worker_disk_p95`, `gate_copy_p95`, `repo_checkout_bytes`, `fixed_run_peak_bytes`, `merge_peak_p95`, `capsule_peak_p95`, `scheduler_jitter_p99_ms`, `gate_setup_duration_p95_ms`, `gate_duration_p95_ms`, sample/evidence refs, and `calibrated_at`. All quantities are bytes or milliseconds and nonnegative. Parallel live enablement requires at least three samples for every selected live route. Calibration may select within static bounds but never widen them.

**`data_policy.v1` and `trusted_repo_attestation.v1`**

Data policy requires `policy_id`, `scope:project`, `mode:local_only|approved_remote`, provider/route allowlists, content-class rules for `public`, `repo_source`, `config_metadata`, `sensitive_personal`, `secret`, and `protected`, each action `deny|local_only|remote|remote_redacted`, redaction profile ref, approving actor/authority ref, validity window, and policy version. `secret` and `protected` are always deny; undeclared payloads fail closed. `trusted_repo_policy.v1` is a closed immutable operator-approved artifact with policy ID/version, operator-authority ref, issue/validity times, sorted unique nonempty execution classes drawn only from `intake|research|synthesis|worker|rescue|gate|review|publication`, residual-host-risk statement hash, `acknowledgement_required=true`, and `containment_claim=TRUSTED_REPOSITORY_ONLY_NO_OS_CONTAINMENT`. `trusted_repo_attestation.v1` is closed and immutable with attestation ID, canonical repo identity, base commit/tree, repo-context digest, typed policy ref/hash, byte-equal class set/authority/validity/risk-statement hash, issue time, and `residual_host_risk_acknowledged=true`. The mapping is exact: intake model calls use `intake`; search, fetch, and research-model calls use `research`; synthesis-model calls use `synthesis`; worker process/model execution uses `worker`; rescue and repair calls use `rescue`; gate proof execution uses `gate`; AI/external review uses `review`; and publication planning or execution uses `publication`. Before an action, the current non-revoked attestation must match repository/base/context/policy/time and include that class. Missing, expired, revoked, mismatched, unacknowledged, or class-incomplete evidence returns NEO_PREFLIGHT_FAILED before execution or disclosure. This is trusted-repository admission on a trusted host and never claims operating-system containment.

`redaction_record.v1` requires source ref/hash, redaction-profile ref/version, matches `[{content_class,field_or_byte_locator,replacement_token}]`, secret-match count without secret values, output ref/hash, actor, and time; unchanged output still records an empty match set. `disclosure_record.v1` requires call/request ID, data-policy ref/hash, provider, route, input content classes, source ref/hash, redacted payload ref/hash or null, redaction-record ref or null, decision `ALLOW_LOCAL|ALLOW_REMOTE|DENY`, authority ref, decided time, and denial reason|null. Every remote `llm_call_record.v1` references an ALLOW_REMOTE disclosure; a denial has no external call. Neither record contains credential or secret values.
